items.title: fix: resolve site application by organization
items.body:
### Description

Fix the Site forward-auth callback so it resolves the application by
`organization + name` instead of `site.owner + name`.

Applications are stored with `owner = "admin"` and `organization = "<org>"`,
while a Site's owner is the organization selected in the UI. The callback
currently calls `GetApplication(site.Owner + "/" + app)`, so it looks for
`<org>/<app>` and returns `the application does not exist` even though
`admin/<app>` exists. The initial login redirect works because it uses the cached
`site.ApplicationObj`, which is why the failure only appears after login.

This change:

- adds `object.GetApplicationByOrganizationAndName(organization, name)`;
- uses it in `handleSiteCallback`, with `site.ApplicationObj` as a fallback;
- adds `Site.MatchesApplication` so the fallback only accepts an application
  from the Site's organization, the Site owner, or a shared application;
- indexes the Site cache by `organization/name` and prefers that key, keeping
  the by-name key as a fallback for shared applications;
- clears the cached `ApplicationObj` before a refresh so a deleted or renamed
  application cannot stay attached to a Site.

Fixes #6009

### How has this been tested?

- `go build ./...` — passed.
- `go test ./object -run TestSiteMatchesApplication` — passed.
- End-to-end callback test against a copy of a real Casdoor database:
  - built a patched v4.24.0 binary and ran it against a copy of the production
    Postgres database (production itself was not touched);
  - old image: `POST /api/forward-auth` with `X-Forwarded-Uri: /caswaf-handler?code=test&state=/`
    returned `Casdoor site error: the application: web_app does not exist`;
  - patched image: the same request reached the token exchange and returned
    `casdoorClient.GetOAuthToken() error: invalid_grant`, proving the application
    was resolved and the callback progressed past the owner lookup.

- [ ] CLA signed
- [x] One commit
- [x] PR title / commit message in lowercase Conventional Commits
- [x] Linked issue (`Fixes #6009`)
- [x] No database schema changes
- [x] New test file has the Apache license header

items.title: OIDC Back-Channel Logout notifications are not sent
items.body:
Back-Channel Logout used to work in version `v3.158.0` but is broken in the current version. Application 2 does not receive a `POST /backchanel-logout` request when user logged out from Application 1.

## Root cause

The issue was introduced by 39ab84b `fix: revoke OAuth tokens when their login session is deleted`.
This commit added `SessionId` to tokens and introduced `ExpireTokensBySessionIds()`, then invoked it from session deletion paths. The token revocation itself is valid, but it changed the ordering assumption used by back-channel logout.

`/api/logout` sends the back-channel notifications too late:

1. `Logout()` clears the Casdoor session and calls `deleteUserSession()`.
2. `deleteUserSession()` calls `DeleteUserSessionId()`.
3. `DeleteUserSessionId()` calls `ExpireTokensBySessionIds()` and sets `expires_in = 0` for all OAuth tokens minted by that Beego session. This can include tokens for Application 1 and Application 2.
4. `Logout()` then calls `SendBackchannelLogout()`.
5. `SendBackchannelLogout()` discovers target applications through `GetActiveTokensByUser()`, which only returns tokens where `expires_in > 0`.

By the time notification discovery runs, Application 2's token has already been expired, so Application 2 is omitted and no POST is made.

## Suggested fix

Send back-channel logout notifications before revoking tokens or deleting the Beego session.

For the no `id_token_hint` branch of `Logout()`:

```go
bcOwner, bcUsername := util.GetOwnerAndNameFromIdNoCheck(user)
object.SendBackchannelLogout(bcOwner, bcUsername, "", c.Ctx.Request.Host)

c.ClearUserSession()
c.ClearTokenSession()
if err := c.deleteUserSession(user, beegoSessionId); err != nil {
    // existing error handling
}
```

For the `id_token_hint` branch, obtain the token and application first, send the notification while the user's other tokens are still active, and only then expire the hinted token and delete the session.

items.title: Reliable security event capture and delivery on top of existing webhooks
items.body:
### Problem

We are designing an integration in which Casdoor is the central identity provider and downstream applications maintain their own local sessions. When an account is disabled/deleted or a session is revoked, applications need an authenticated change notification and a recoverable delivery path.

This is a follow-up to the existing webhook work, not a request to add retries from scratch. #5037 was addressed by #5337, and #5344 added further improvements. The persistent WebhookEvent records, delivery worker, failure inspection, and replay API are useful foundations.

Source observations at master `d61ee823196151e9c282d497a78ec66a800ea91f`:

- [UpdateUser](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/d61ee823196151e9c282d497a78ec66a800ea91f/object/user.go#L1008) persists the user change before calling access termination.
- [AddRecord](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/d61ee823196151e9c282d497a78ec66a800ea91f/object/record.go#L240) invokes SendWebhooks and logs an error if event creation fails; [AddWebhookEvent](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/d61ee823196151e9c282d497a78ec66a800ea91f/object/webhook_event.go#L171) inserts through the database engine separately. Retrying existing webhook rows does not recover a security event that was never captured after the identity change.
- [OIDC back-channel logout](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/d61ee823196151e9c282d497a78ec66a800ea91f/object/token_logout.go#L81) is a separate path: it selects applications from active token records and starts a one-off HTTP request in a goroutine. A relying party may still have a local session after its upstream access token has expired.
- A generic API audit record, a session-logout request, and a committed account-disabled event have different meanings. Integrators currently have to reconstruct these distinctions.

The requested improvement is a supported contract for reliably capturing security-relevant state changes and delivering them to the appropriate applications.

### Proposed solution

For an initial increment, focus on account disable/re-enable/delete and explicit session revocation, reusing the existing webhook infrastructure where practical.

1. **Reliable capture at the source.** A committed, supported identity-state change should leave a durable event that survives a crash before network delivery. A rolled-back change should not publish a successful state-change event. A transactional outbox is one possible implementation; an equivalent mechanism would also work. Document which native admin/API mutation paths are covered.
2. **Explicit event semantics and stable identity.** Include an event ID, event type, issuer and stable subject identifier, occurrence time, and sufficient version/ordering information for receivers to handle stale events. Preserve the minimal subject information required to deliver a deletion event after the user row is gone. Distinguish account disablement from ordinary logout.
3. **Explicit receiver scope.** Authorize receivers for the applications and subjects they are entitled to observe. Security-event coverage should not depend only on an unexpired access-token row when the receiver still has a valid local session.
4. **Recoverable per-receiver delivery.** Reuse persisted tasks, configurable backoff, visible failed/dead-letter records, and replay. Document retention, expiry, and administrative discard behavior. Successfully captured events retained under that policy should support at-least-once delivery; receivers must deduplicate by stable event ID. The multi-instance worker concern already mentioned in #5344 could be a separate follow-up.
5. **Clear acknowledgment semantics.** Specify that a receiver acknowledges successful delivery only after validation and durable acceptance. Transport acceptance should remain distinct from completion of downstream business actions such as revoking every local session. Receiver-side processing and recovery remain the receiver's responsibility.

Standards alignment with OpenID SSF / CAEP / RISC would be valuable, while a complete SSF implementation need not be a prerequisite for the first increment. Existing OIDC logout semantics and security-event semantics should stay distinct even if they share delivery infrastructure.

### Alternatives considered

- **Periodic introspection:** usable when the endpoint authoritatively reflects the required account/session state, but changes are discovered on a subsequent check and ongoing access gains an additional online dependency.
- **Application-side retry queues:** useful after an event arrives, but unable to recover an event that was never recorded or sent by the identity provider.
- **A custom administrative wrapper:** can persist an operation before calling Casdoor, but requires all relevant writes to go through that wrapper; native admin/API changes outside it remain a separate integration problem. A supported source-side capability would avoid every integration rebuilding this behavior.

As an architectural reference, Keycloak's [experimental SSF support](https://www.keycloak.org/2026/07/experimental-ssf-support) describes transactional event capture and asynchronous delivery. Its [current guide](https://www.keycloak.org/securing-apps/ssf-support) explicitly marks the feature experimental and unsuitable for production; this is a design reference, not a claim of a production-ready equivalent.

### Additional context

Suggested validation scenarios:

- Commit an account change, then stop the process before the HTTP delivery; delivery resumes from persisted state after restart.
- Roll back the account change; no successful change event is delivered.
- Keep a receiver unavailable, restore it, and verify retry/replay with stable IDs; a lost acknowledgment and repeated delivery remain safe.
- Disable and then re-enable an account while delivery is delayed; the event contract lets the receiver reject stale state updates, using versions or an authoritative state check.
- Keep a relying party's local session active after its upstream access token expires; a registered security-event receiver still receives an applicable disablement/revocation event.

Related work: #5037, #5337, #5344. Relevant delivery standard: [RFC 8935](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8935.html).

Would the maintainers consider extending the existing webhook subsystem in this direction, and which source-side capture approach best fits Casdoor's architecture?

items.body:
Hello! Currently, when users are synced from an LDAP server to Casdoor, they remain in Casdoor even if they are deleted on the LDAP side. This can lead to inconsistencies and outdated user information in Casdoor.

### Feature Request:

Add a feature to automatically remove users from Casdoor if they are no longer present in the synced LDAP directory. This could be implemented as:

1. **Automatic Sync**: During each synchronization cycle, Casdoor would compare the current LDAP users with those in Casdoor and automatically delete any users not found in LDAP.
2. **Manual Sync Option**: Provide an option to trigger this cleanup manually through the Casdoor UI or API.
3. **Soft Delete Option**: To prevent accidental data loss, provide an option to "soft delete" users initially by deactivating them rather than permanently removing them.
4. **Logging & Notifications**: Keep a log of all deletions and optionally send notifications to administrators when users are deleted through this sync process.

### Use Case:

When an employee leaves a company and their LDAP account is deleted, this feature would ensure that their access to Casdoor-protected applications is automatically revoked without manual intervention.

### Benefits:

- Reduces manual work for administrators.
- Keeps Casdoor in sync with the actual state of the LDAP directory.

Upgrading to the official `casbin/casdoor:4.4.0` image fails during database initialization with MySQL Error 1118 when adding `user.password_history`. The official `4.3.0` image starts successfully against the same restored database.

I also reproduced the failing DDL using **only the user table schema, with zero rows**, on an isolated MySQL container. No application data is required.

### Environment

- Casdoor: existing database from `3.128.0`; `4.3.0` starts successfully; `4.4.0` fails.
- Production database: Google Cloud SQL for MySQL `9.7.1-google`.
- Independent schema-only reproduction: official `mysql:8.4.10` Docker image.
- InnoDB, `ROW_FORMAT=Dynamic`, `utf8mb4`, `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`.
- `innodb_strict_mode=ON`.
- Existing primary key: `owner VARCHAR(100), name VARCHAR(255)`.

The 4.4.0 container panics during `object.(*Ormer).createTable` / schema synchronization:

```text
panic: Error 1118 (42000): Row size too large (> 8126). Changing some columns to TEXT or BLOB may help. In current row format, BLOB prefix of 0 bytes is stored inline.
```

items.body:
Implements HTTP reverse proxy functionality adapted from CasWAF. Incoming requests are routed to backend services based on Host header matching against Application's `domain` field.

## Implementation

**Domain-to-Application cache** (`object/application_cache.go`)
- In-memory map with RWMutex for concurrent access
- Auto-refreshes on application CRUD operations
- O(1) lookup, no database queries in request path

**Proxy handler** (`proxy/reverse_proxy.go`)
- Routes requests via `httputil.ReverseProxy` to Application's `upstreamHost`
- Returns 404 for unmapped domains or missing upstream configuration
- Sets standard headers: `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host`
- Preserves WebSocket upgrade headers

**Configuration** (`conf/app.conf`)
```ini
proxyHttpPort = 80        # HTTP proxy listener (empty = disabled)
proxyHttpsPort =          # HTTPS listener (prepared for future use)
```

**Usage**
```bash
# Configure application
Domain: blog.example.com
UpstreamHost: localhost:3000

# Requests to blog.example.com:80 → localhost:3000
curl -H 'Host: blog.example.com' http://proxy:80/api/users
```

## Architecture

Proxy runs on separate port from Beego API (default 8000). The lookup function is injected into the proxy package to avoid import cycles between `object` and `proxy`.

HTTPS/TLS termination deferred - requires certificate handling from Application's `sslCert` field.

items.title: Add support for cross-application session deletion in SSO setups
items.body:
Currently `DeleteSession` only removes sessions for a specific `(owner, name, application)` tuple. In SSO environments where users authenticate once across multiple applications, logout only invalidates one application's session, leaving others active.

## Changes

**Backend API (`object/session.go`)**
- Add `DeleteAllSessions bool` field to `Session` struct (non-persisted, API only)
- Modify `DeleteSession(id string, deleteAllSessions bool)` with conditional logic:
  - `true`: Query and delete all sessions matching `(owner, name)` across applications
  - `false`: Preserve existing single-application deletion behavior
- Delete from beego session store before database to prevent inconsistent state

**Controller (`controllers/session.go`)**
- Pass `session.DeleteAllSessions` from request body to `object.DeleteSession()`

**User deletion (`object/user.go`)**
- Call `DeleteSession(id, true)` to clear all sessions when user is removed

## Usage

```javascript
// Single-application logout (existing behavior, default)
deleteSession({ owner, name, application })

// SSO logout across all applications
deleteSession({ owner, name, application, deleteAllSessions: true })
```

Backward compatible: omitting `deleteAllSessions` defaults to `false`.

items.title: [feature] Add reverse proxy (HTTP/HTTPS forwarding) by reusing CasWAF's proxy code
items.body:
### Background

After extending the `Application` object with reverse proxy fields (see #XXXX), this issue implements the actual reverse proxy functionality. The core logic should be ported from [CasWAF](https://github.com/casbin/caswaf)'s `proxy/` and `service/` packages. The goal is to make Casdoor work like Nginx: receive HTTP requests on a public port, match the `Host` header to an Application's `Domain`, and forward the request to the configured upstream `ProxyHost:ProxyPort`.

### Key code to reuse from CasWAF

- **`service/proxy.go`** — contains the main reverse proxy handler using Go's `net/http/httputil.ReverseProxy`. Reference: https://github.com/casbin/caswaf/blob/master/service/proxy.go
- **`proxy/`** — helper utilities for proxy handling
- **Domain matching logic** — looks up the incoming request's `Host` header against all configured `Site.Domain` values to find the correct backend

### What to implement

1. **Port CasWAF's reverse proxy handler to Casdoor**
   - Create a new package (e.g., `proxy/`) in Casdoor
   - Implement a `http.Handler` that:
     1. Reads the `Host` header from the incoming request
     2. Looks up the matching `Application` by its `Domain` (or `OtherDomains`) field
     3. If found, forwards the request to `ProxyHost:ProxyPort` using `httputil.ReverseProxy`
     4. If not found, returns 404 or passes through to the normal Beego handler
   - Port the relevant helper functions from CasWAF's `service/proxy.go`

2. **Start a separate HTTP listener for the proxy**
   - The proxy should listen on a configurable port (e.g., `80` for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS), separate from the Beego API port (default `8000`)
   - Add configuration in `conf/app.conf`: `proxyPort = 80` (default empty = proxy disabled)
   - When `proxyPort` is configured, Casdoor starts an additional HTTP listener on that port

3. **Request header handling**
   - Set standard reverse proxy headers: `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host`
   - Support WebSocket upgrade (pass through `Upgrade` and `Connection` headers), as CasWAF does

4. **Application lookup caching**
   - Cache the `Domain → Application` mapping in memory for performance
   - Refresh cache when an Application is created/updated/deleted

### Non-goals (separate issues)

- HTTPS / TLS termination (handled by the cert issue)
- WAF rules / firewall (not needed in Casdoor)
- OAuth proxy (Casdoor already has its own auth; this is not needed at the proxy layer for now)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When an Application has `Domain=blog.example.com` and `ProxyHost=localhost:3000`, HTTP requests to `blog.example.com` on the proxy port are forwarded to `localhost:3000`
- [ ] Proxy headers (`X-Forwarded-For`, etc.) are correctly set
- [ ] Applications without `Domain` configured are not affected
- [ ] The Beego API port continues to work independently

### References

- CasWAF proxy handler: https://github.com/casbin/caswaf/blob/master/service/proxy.go
- CasWAF overview (reverse proxy): https://caswaf.org/docs/overview/

items.body:
- [x] Analyze the codebase and identify the performance issue
- [x] Identify that syncUsers() fetches all users on every sync cycle
- [x] Understand the Syncer struct and synchronization mechanism
- [x] Add LastSyncTime field to Syncer struct
- [x] Modify getOriginalUsers() to support incremental sync with timestamp filtering
- [x] Update syncUsers() to use incremental sync when possible
- [x] Update syncer after successful sync to record LastSyncTime
- [x] Add tests for incremental sync functionality
- [x] Test the changes to ensure backward compatibility
- [x] Verify performance improvements with documentation
- [x] Run security review of changes
- [x] Clean up build artifacts
- [x] Add inline code documentation
- [x] Create comprehensive implementation summary
- [x] Fix duplicate key constraint violation when IsReadOnly=false with incremental sync

## Summary

Successfully implemented incremental synchronization for the Casdoor syncer to resolve performance issues with large user datasets (50,000+ users).

### Recent Fix (commit 657decc)
Fixed a critical bug where incremental sync with `IsReadOnly=false` caused duplicate key violations. The issue occurred because:
- In incremental sync mode, `myOUsers` only contains recently modified users from external DB
- The code was checking ALL local users against this partial set
- Users not in the partial set were incorrectly assumed to be missing from external DB
- Attempting to add them caused `duplicate key value violates unique constraint` errors

**Solution**: Only sync new local users to external database during full sync. During incremental sync, we skip this step since we don't have the complete external user list to compare against.

### Problem Statement
During periodic synchronization with large user counts, Casdoor fetched and compared ALL users on every sync cycle, causing:
- High CPU usage from processing 50,000+ comparisons
- High I/O load from querying entire tables
- Increased memory consumption
- Long sync times proportional to total user count

### Solution
Implemented an **automatic incremental sync mechanism** that:
- Only fetches users modified since the last successful sync
- Reduces processing load by up to 500x for typical workloads
- Activates automatically when conditions are met
- Is fully backward compatible with existing configurations
- Properly handles IsReadOnly=false mode

### Technical Changes

#### Files Modified (538 lines added):
1. **object/syncer.go** - Added LastSyncTime field and helper functions
2. **object/syncer_sync.go** - Enhanced syncUsers() with incremental sync logic and fixed IsReadOnly bug
3. **object/syncer_user.go** - Added filtered query capability
4. **object/syncer_incremental_test.go** (NEW) - Comprehensive unit tests
5. **.gitignore** - Added build artifact patterns
6. **INCREMENTAL_SYNC.md** (NEW) - User-facing documentation
7. **IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md** (NEW) - Technical implementation guide

#### Key Functions:
- `getUpdatedTimeColumn()` - Finds UpdatedTime column in table mappings
- `getOriginalUsersWithFilter()` - Queries only modified users
- `updateSyncerLastSyncTime()` - Records timestamp after successful sync

### How It Works

**Automatic Detection:**
```go
useIncrementalSync := syncer.LastSyncTime != "" && syncer.getUpdatedTimeColumn() != ""
```

**When Incremental Sync is Used:**
- LastSyncTime exists (from previous sync)
- External table has UpdatedTime column mapped
- Result: Query becomes `WHERE updated_at > last_sync_time`
- Skips syncing local users to external DB (only done in full sync)

**When Full Sync is Used:**
- First sync (no LastSyncTime yet)
- No UpdatedTime column in table
- Result: Query fetches all users as before
- Syncs new local users to external DB when IsReadOnly=false

### Performance Impact

**Example: 50,000 users, 100 modified per hour**
- **Before**: Queries 50,000 users, processes 50,000 comparisons every sync
- **After**: Queries 100 users, processes 100 comparisons every sync
- **Improvement**: ~500x reduction in processing load

### Security
✅ **SQL Injection Prevention**: Uses parameterized queries
✅ **Input Validation**: Column names from admin config, timestamps from system
✅ **Access Control**: Maintains existing security model
✅ **No New Vulnerabilities**: Manual security review completed

### Testing
✅ **Unit Tests**: 3 new tests, all passing
✅ **Build**: Compiles without errors or warnings
✅ **Code Quality**: Passes go vet and go fmt
✅ **Backward Compatibility**: Existing syncers work unchanged
✅ **Bug Fix Validated**: Duplicate key error resolved

### Configuration

To enable incremental sync, add UpdatedTime mapping in syncer configuration:
```json
{
  "tableColumns": [
    {
      "name": "updated_at",
      "casdoorName": "UpdatedTime"
    }
  ]
}
```

No configuration changes required - feature works automatically when conditions are met!

### Monitoring

Check logs to see which mode is active:
```
Using incremental sync (last sync: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z)
Users: 50000, oUsers: 100
```

### Documentation
- **INCREMENTAL_SYNC.md**: User guide with configuration, troubleshooting, examples
- **IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md**: Technical details, architecture, security analysis
- **Inline comments**: Code-level documentation for maintainability

- ✅ Duplicate key bug fixed

items.title: encountered several issues and potential improvements in the user synchronization mechanism
items.body:
We have encountered several issues and potential improvements in the user synchronization mechanism in Casdoor, especially when dealing with large datasets (e.g., 50,000+ users) and two-way sync scenarios.

Problems Observed:

Last Sync Time Persistence
Currently, the last synchronization timestamp is stored in the database. It might be better to keep this value in a temporary in-memory variable or cache, so that in case of partial failures or system restarts, the system can recover gracefully without database corruption or inconsistent states.

High Resource Consumption During Full Sync
During a full synchronization, Casdoor consumes a large amount of CPU and memory. It would be more efficient if the sync process runs in batches (for example, handling insert and update operations in groups of N users) to reduce system load and improve throughput.

Incremental Sync Conflict in Two-Way Synchronization
The current incremental sync logic fails (not work) when a user is added directly in Casdoor’s database.In two-way synchronization setups, this causes missing or unsynchronized users.

User Deletion Synchronization
When a user is deleted from the external system (connected application), it would be ideal if Casdoor could also remove the corresponding user entry from its own database. This ensures that both sides remain consistent and synchronized.

Suggested Improvements:

Use in-memory or cached storage for temporary sync states (like last sync time).
Implement batch-based full sync for large-scale user imports.
Improve incremental sync logic to handle bidirectional updates and additions.
Add synchronization for deletions to keep databases consistent.
